headline: Bahrain Appeals to Security Council After Reported Drone Episode
deck: Bahrain invoked Article 51 and appealed to the Security Council; U.S. and Bahraini authorities had not confirmed the claimed radar hit.
body: Bahrain’s Foreign Ministry said Iranian drones had been intercepted and destroyed in its airspace on Sunday, after what it described as a similar two-drone attack on Friday [E1]. The ministry rejected the Iranian Revolutionary Guard’s stated pretexts and held Iran responsible for the attacks and their consequences [E2].

Bahrain’s statement said it retained an individual and collective right of self-defense under Article 51, referred to the Gulf Cooperation Council’s Joint Defense Agreement, and called on the Security Council to condemn the attacks and take measures under Resolution 2817 [E3]. The paper’s 28 June Gulf-strikes coverage described claimed Iranian hits on U.S. sites and subsequent U.S. strikes; this statement adds Bahrain’s stated Article 51 and Security Council appeal.

Anadolu Agency reported that Bahrain said its air defenses had intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks [E7]. It reported that Bahrain said they were destroyed before reaching their targets [E8].

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it had targeted a United States radar site at Bahrain’s al-Riffa Air Base with six drones [E9]. RFE/RL reported the same claim through Iranian state media [E10].

RFE/RL reported no immediate confirmation from U.S. or Bahraini authorities that the radar installation had been hit [E11]. It also reported that the U.S. military had previously said it intercepted two Iranian drones targeting the island, with no casualties or damage [E12].

Saudi Arabia condemned the aerial attacks after the IRGC claim [E4]. Saudi Arabia said it stood with Bahrain over measures to protect its security and stability [E5], and called for an immediate halt to Iranian attacks on countries in the region [E6].

The Guardian introduced Bahrain’s ministry statement as describing drone strikes that were intercepted and shot down [E13]. It reported that Jordan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Qatar expressed solidarity with Bahrain [E14]. The Guardian also reported that continued attacks would complicate efforts to contain tension and undermine diplomatic work toward regional security and stability [E15].

evidence_box.fragment: The Bahraini Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed the Kingdom of Bahrain’s strongest condemnation of the continued Iranian aggression against its territory, including the attack launched today, Sunday, November 15, 2026, by drones that were intercepted and destroyed by air defense systems in the Kingdom’s airspace. This comes two days after a similar attack at dawn on Friday, November 13, 2026, by two drones that were also intercepted.

evidence_box.fragment: The Ministry affirmed the Kingdom of Bahrain’s categorical rejection of the flimsy pretexts and false claims put forward by the Iranian Revolutionary Guard, stressing that no pretext justifies aggression against the sovereignty of states and the integrity of their territories, and that freedom of navigation and passage, by sea and air, in the straits used for international navigation is a right guaranteed by the rules of international law, and is not subject to the will or conditions of any state. It also rejects turning its territory into an arena for settling scores, and holds Iran fully responsible for these attacks and their consequences.

evidence_box.fragment: The Ministry also affirmed that the Kingdom of Bahrain retains its inherent right, both individually and collectively, to self-defense in accordance with Article (51) of the Charter, and to take all necessary measures to preserve its sovereignty and the security of its citizens and residents on its land, in close coordination with its brothers in the Cooperation Council for the Arab States of the Gulf, based on the Joint Defense Agreement, which considers an attack on any member state as an attack on all of them, and with its allies and partners. The Ministry noted that the Kingdom of Bahrain, as a member of the UN Security Council, calls on the Council to condemn these repeated attacks, and demands that it assume its responsibilities and take decisive measures to ensure Iran’s full compliance with Resolution 2817, and to stop its attacks, threats and support for proxy groups in the region.
